A good fridge (better brand) will last 15-20 years if you're lucky. I don't know how fancy yours is but, it's probably going to cost you $400 to get it fixed. For twice that you can easily replace it. Also as an aside, if you own your home you should have a whole house surge suppressor system installed at the electric panel, this is going to help save all sorts of stuff in your house.

My thoughts (having repaired several of my own fridges):

When the door was left open, the coils iced over. There's a built-in defroster, but that kind of situation can cause the drain to ice up and just generally stay iced up and not really functional. I'd be willing to bet that if you had a thermometer in your fridge you'd see that it's a good 10deg warmer than "normal" (and probably outside of the safe zone). The freezer is more demanding and that's why it seems like the fridge is working but not the freezer. Unless you have a Samsung (the only dual units I know of, though there are likely others), then the whole machine runs off one condenser/set of coils.

As for what to do, I'd defrost the unit. That means pulling EVERYTHING out and storing it elsewhere for a day. Chances are good that most of the food in the fridge is compromised, condiments being on the safer end and animal products (eggs, milk, uncooked meat) on the less safe end. Anything that was in the freezer and became even partially thawed, I'd consider "suspect". Anyway, with the unit defrosted for a day, I'd be willing to bet that it'll work again just fine.

If you go this route, do some maintenance on it as well. There are cooling fins under the bottom of the fridge that tend to get clogged with dust and dirt. This hurts the efficiency, wastes money and makes the unit work longer (harder) which shortens the life. Clean those coils/fins.

15 year old fridge though? Might be time to think about buying new. The EPA claims that at 15 years you're using twice as much energy to achieve the same end. Or not, when my folks sold the home I grew up in, I had to help them move a fridge from the basement that had been there for ~40 years and they had moved with them to the house... it worked fine and there was no reason for them to replace it so they didn't.

Luckily, we are down to the wire with food - should have gone to the grocery store earlier this week, but work has been too busy for it (sucks bc I've just 'eating' protein shakes and salads from the garden all week).

I've got another 12-hour day, and had talked with my fiance about what to do last night, so he's ready to go buy another fridge today once he wakes up. Either way, aside from chicken and fish in the freezer, I think we can swing putting the freezer goods in the fridge (flour, butter, some ground beef, frozen veggies) until the problem is resolved.

Maybe it is time for a new one. We have been cutting back on electricity use, but our KWH readings have been the same as last year so maybe the fridge is the culprit. Thank you so much for your input! We'll try the maintenance/defrost and at least for now we can put getting a new one on hold.

Wish I could upvote you again! I went ahead and defrosted it and the heating element was totally gone. I also followed your advice and cleaned everything in the back, took the fan out for the condenser and inspected it, also figured out why my damned icemaker stopped working and got the doors flush again (fridge side was lower than freezer, have not replaced cams but will look at those next month). You saved me about $1600 with your advice.

I'm hoping with the work done, it will last another five years or so. Also told the family we have to pull it out monthly and clean the coils (there was a TON of pet hair somehow down in the coils).

No problem, I'm always happy when I can help someone. :) I think a monthly cleaning is overkill, yearly is common and yours was probably the full 15 year lifespan.

For whatever it's worth, there are a few appliance repair forums worth their salt (who also sell parts), I tend to default to RepairClinic.com because I can get most items next day with standard shipping (close warehouse). Good place to get parts and advice if you need either.
